full_judgment:
This Revisional application arises out of Family Suit No. 13 of 1993 of the court of Assistant Judge and Family Court, Parbatipur, Dinajpur and is directed against the judgment and decree dated 9-11-1994 passed by the Additional District Judge, Dinajpur in Family Appeal No. 34 of 1993 affirming the judgment and decree dated 10-11-1993 passed by the Family Judge in Family Suit No. 13 of 1993. 

 4. The suit was tried by the learned Assistant Judge and Family Court, Parbatipur and by his judgment and decree dated 10-11-1993, decreed, the suit. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendant petitioner preferred an appeal before the District Judge, Dinajpur and on transfer the same appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge who vide his judgment and decree dated 9-11-1994 was pleased to dismiss the appeal in Family Appeal No. 34 of 1994 affirming the Judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in Family Suit No. 13 of 1993. The defendant petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of affirmance passed by the Addl. District Judge, Dinajpur preferred this revisional application and obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court below concurred with the finding of the trial Court that the dower at the time of marriage was fixed at Taka 37,985.00 out of which a nose ring valued at Taka 100.00 was paid by the defendant petitioner at the time of solemnisation of the marriage and, as such, arrived at a definite finding that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 is entitled to get Taka 37,825.00 on account of her dower and in arriving at such finding the appellate Court below took into consideration that the testimony of DWs. cannot be relied on because the defendant petitioner himself has given two different versions in respect of amount of dower and the evidence adduced by the DWs. are conflicting with the assertions made by the defendant petitioner in his written statement and in that view of the matter, both the courts below did not put any reliance on the evidence of DWs. On the other hand, both the courts below found that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 as PW 1 has fully reiterated her case in evidence as PW 1 and her testimony has been corroborated by the other PWs. and the evidence of PWs. could not be shaken in cross examination. Both the courts below further observed that they did not find anything on record to disbelieve the testimony of the PWs. and, as such, they have put reliance on the evidence of PWs. and arrived at a finding that the dower was fixed at Taka 37,925.00 and this concurrent finding of fact arrived at by the courts below are based on materials and evidence on record and in that view of the matter this court sitting under revisional jurisdiction has no scope to disturb this finding which is based on cogent materials and evidence on record. Here it may further be mentioned that both the courts below concurrently found that the maintenance at the rate of Taka 400.00 per month in respect of minor child has been found to be reasonable and Mr. Sajjat Ali Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner, did not assail this portion of the impugned judgment, rather he has frankly conceded that there is nothing on record to assail the finding of the courts below on the point of maintenance, given in respect of minor child. It further appears that the trial Court below after analysing the case of both the parties and considering the evidence on record arrived at a finding that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 is entitled to get maintenance in respect of her minor child unless and until she attains puberty and the defendant petitioner is bound to maintain the minor child and he has also found that an amount of Taka 400.00 per month is reasonable amount and in that view of the matter the learned appellate Court below concurred with the finding of the trial Court also on the point of maintenance. It may further be mentioned that Mr. Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party, has rightly submitted that the PW 2 is not a disinterested witness rather he is an interested witness who happens to be uncle of the defendant petitioner and his conduct is not beyond question. It is found that the DW 2 has been removed from Imamship and, as such, both the courts below rightly discarded the evidence of this DW along with other DWs. So I find nothing on record to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court below.
